boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Chancellorsville Campaign [April-May 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Chancellorsville April 30–May 6, Fredericksburg II May 3 and Salem Church May 3–4, 1863. VA033 and VA034 lie inside VA032's frozen interval; campaign-wide loss tables and Sixth Corps totals span more than one engagement and must not be added or assigned. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Corps; the live field reads zero. NPS says the VI Corps, reinforced by Gibbon's division, assaulted outnumbered Confederates. Sedgwick says the enemy's works were occupied in considerable force; Early says Barksdale's Mississippians held the trenches at the foot of Marye's Hill.
claims.rationale: No count is given for either side; none is adopted. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Sedgwick says his order to cross at Fredericksburg found his whole command south of the river, where no bridges had been laid at the town, so he moved by the flank on the Bowling Green road instead of recrossing. Early says part of Pendleton's artillery had been sent to the rear under instructions.
claims.rationale: Movement statements from the two opposing reports; no inspected engineer or artillery record.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sedgwick says the storming columns carried the works, capturing guns and many prisoners; Early says the trenches were carried and the hill taken, with much of the 18th and part of the 21st Mississippi and a company of the Washington Artillery captured; NPS says the Confederates withdrew and regrouped.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,000 total; the live field reads zero. Sedgwick's 4,925 covers all Sixth Corps operations, and Early's division loss of 136 killed, 838 wounded and some 500 missing covers the whole period from the crossing, excluding Barksdale's brigade and the artillery.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Both report totals span Salem Church (VA033) and more; neither is assigned to this engagement.

open_questions: Barksdale's, Griffin's, Gibbon's and Newton's reports and any engagement-specific return remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded a division at Chancellorsville) whose figures partly rest on others' estimates. Lee's, Sedgwick's and Early's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXV, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
